fort_courtyard.label: Travancore fort courtyard in a sea squall
fort_courtyard.anchor: The inner courtyard of the red laterite Travancore coastal fort: laterite walls and sloping tiled roofs, a powder store where men drag oiled cloth over barrels, puddled mud and a low doorway in an inner wall. Over the far wall a grey squall line drives in from the sea.
fort_courtyard.absent: No ships, foreign bastions, stone castle towers or European soldiers, and no musket fire or battle. The abandoned plan board carries no writing or numerals.
fort_courtyard.time: afternoon under a bruised sky as the squall breaks into sheeting rain

archive_room.label: Ramayyan's palm-leaf archive room
archive_room.anchor: A long, narrow room inside the fort's inner wall, wooden shelves from floor to ceiling packed with string-tied palm-leaf bundles, each hung with a small clay tag bearing only abstract impressed marks, the rows receding into shadow. The floor is swept bare, one high narrow window gives the only daylight, and a small coconut-oil lamp with an open wick burns on a low wooden table at the centre, used from the floor; each man sits or stands as his panel describes, and in every two-shot Nagoji keeps frame left and Ramayyan frame right.
archive_room.absent: No chairs, stools, desks, bound books, paper scrolls, glass lamps or lanterns, and no dust or cobwebs. No script, numerals or symbols on tags, leaves or cover boards, and no third person in the room except a ghosted figure where a panel's memory bleed asks for one.
archive_room.time: rainy afternoon: cool grey light from the high window and the small warm lamp flame

pune_memory.label: Maratha sardar's hall in Pune, remembered
pune_memory.anchor: A Maratha sardar's audience hall in Pune years earlier, seen from behind a carved wooden lattice screen: carved teak pillars, lime-plastered walls, white floor spreads and bolsters, the sardar seated in judgement with the astrologer beside him and the kneeling captain in the foreground. The view is the narrator's own eyes, with no observer in frame.
pune_memory.absent: No coast, coconut palms or Kerala tiled roofs, no Nagoji, no rust-red turban with a red sash, and no throne or European chair. No blade stroke, wound or blood, only the executioner's shadow across the captain, and the astrologer never has the temple priest's face.
pune_memory.time: hard Deccan daylight broken by the lattice, faded like an old memory

festival_memory.label: Festival night at Padmanabhapuram, remembered
festival_memory.anchor: A granite-flagged inner courtyard at Padmanabhapuram, closed in by carved teak and laterite palace buildings under steep sloping tiled roofs with timber gables, with a small shrine at the far end where priests chant. Rows of small clay and brass open-wick lamps line the foot of the walls, and a crowd of men and women in plain white cloth presses close in a ring.
festival_memory.absent: No tall stone gateway tower, glass lanterns or European figures, and no crown, turban or crest on the king. No blood or wounds, and the narrator is never shown with a face.
festival_memory.time: dusk turning to night in one warm lamp palette

estate_courtyard.label: Jackfruit tree in Nagoji's estate courtyard
estate_courtyard.anchor: The courtyard of Nagoji's Travancore estate: a raised stone platform built round the trunk of a great jackfruit tree, the swept earth yard dried after the rain, the dark tiled roof of the house and the kalari across the yard, and coconut palms beyond the wall toward the sea. Nagoji lies alone on his back on the platform.
estate_courtyard.absent: No chair, bench, cot, companion, lit lamp in the yard, ship or foreign fort. No prison cell, chain or iron.
estate_courtyard.time: night after the rain, the sky clearing to stars

ledger_split.label: Goa ledger beside Ramayyan's leaf
ledger_split.anchor: Two matched halves at one angle and framing, hands only. Left: a bound paper ledger lying flat and square on a rough prison table, a clerk's hand in a dark cuff holding a quill, wet ink and one empty ruled line; right: a palm leaf flat and square on Ramayyan's low table with one empty band, his ink-stained fingers and a stylus.
ledger_split.absent: No faces, full figures, guards, ropes, irons or cell bars. No writing, numerals or marks on either page; the empty line and the empty band stay bare.
ledger_split.time: cold grey prison light on the left half, warm open-wick lamp light on the right half

character_notes.nagoji: Thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin and jaw with no beard or facial scar, and a tiny flush gold ear stud on the lobe with nothing hanging from it. Kerala topknot high on the crown with the first grey at the temples, no turban, cream mundu and shoulder cloth, silver chain of office, the old brand and long white scar on the inner LEFT forearm, and no knife, bandages or coat.
character_notes.ramayyan: Thin clean-shaven face with no moustache, sharp fine features and a high receding hairline with dark curls at the sides and back, as on his sheet; plain unbordered white cloth and ink-stained fingers. No chain, jewellery, forehead marks or sacred thread, never Nagoji's topknot or moustache, and never the temple priest's face.
character_notes.padmini: In her fifties, thick black hair threaded with grey and coiled at the nape; cotton sari hitched for walking in the old Kerala drape with no stitched blouse, simple gold and a long walking stick.
character_notes.revathi: A little younger than Nagoji: deep indigo sari with gold, jasmine in her braid, flat-coin necklace, gold armlets and a thin sandalwood line at the hairline. A tali at her throat and the first grey threading her black hair.
character_notes.eustachius: Tall, with pale hair tied back; a plain white cotton tunic-coat over a shirt and a white ankle-length mundu. Never a uniform, blue coat, tricorne or wig.
character_notes.varma: Face and build from his sheet but younger, with black hair bound back, never the grey of the sheet's older figure. Bare-headed and bare-chested in a plain mundu, with no turban, crest, headband or crown, whatever the sheet shows.
